subject: Model shortlist + trial plan: tradeoffs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finora.com>, Peter Sato <peter@finora.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model shortlist + trial plan: tradeoffs & next steps

Hi Olivia / Peter —

Thanks again for the demo slot today — liked how you walked through the summarization flows and the retrieval examples. Per our conversation I pulled together a short recommended model shortlist, the tradeoffs we should expect, and concrete next steps so we can get a short trial running next week. I attached the run-of-bench CSV and the prompt set we used.

Quick recap / asks from you:
- Latency SLO (p95) for interactive chat: confirm target (you mentioned ~300ms)
- Monthly target spend for initial trial: confirm budget range
- Share a representative sample of the dataset (few thousand rows) or a sanitized example export

Recommended shortlist (initial trial):
1) redwood-lite-6b-quant (default) — best for throughput and cost. Expect p95 < 200ms on our Dedicated config, low token cost. Quality is solid for paraphrase & short summarization; may miss fine-grained factual details on longer docs.
2) redwood-mid-13b-opt (balanced) — middle ground. ~2x cost of 6b, better on hallucination resistance and long-context summarization; p95 ~250-400ms depending on load. Good for mainline customer-facing summaries.
3) redwood-qa-33b (high-quality fallback) — highest quality for nuanced regulatory/legal summaries. 4–6x the cost of 6b and higher latency (p95 600–900ms); recommended as a routed fallback for "critical_intent" queries only.

Proposed trial config (what we'll deploy for the POC):
- Deploy 6b as default serving model (100% traffic initially)
- Canary 13b on 20% traffic for 72 hours to collect quality deltas and compare hallucination rates on the prompt set
- Configure conditional fallback to 33b for labeled critical intents (we can provide rule-based filters to start)
- Run a 48-hour throughput and stability bench with your sample to validate autoscaling profile and billing estimates

Attachments: finora-benchmarks-20270525.csv, finora-prompt-sets-v1.jsonl (prompt examples and evals)
Related links: benchmark dashboard (drive link), trial config template (we'll share)

Next steps I propose:
- Olivia: confirm latency SLO and budget window by EOD Thu (May 27)
- Finora: share a redacted sample dataset or 500–1,000-line CSV for evaluation
- We'll schedule a 45min technical sync after we get the sample to finalize canary rules and fallback logic (proposed slot Tue Jun 1)

If that sounds good I can spin up the trial config and send a DocuSign PO template / trial contract for signatures.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0118

From: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finora.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Peter Sato <peter@finora.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist + trial plan: tradeoffs & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the trial: 

- Latency SLO: yes, our product goal is p95 <= 300ms for core chat flows. For longer summarization jobs (batch) we can tolerate higher latency.
- Budget: initial trial allocation is $12k/month. If the numbers look promising we can scale.
- Critical use cases: one of our top flows is regulatory summarization for audit teams; for those we need very low hallucination risk.
- Compliance: can you confirm whether SOC 2 evidence or an SSP is available for review during the trial? (we may need it for procurement)

Also — can you share concrete metric definitions you plan to collect for the canary? e.g., ROUGE/F1 on our prompt set, hallucination incidence, average tokens per call, and p95 latency.

If you can get me a short written plan for monitoring and an estimate of expected monthly spend for the proposed config (6b default + 20% 13b canary + fallback usage assumptions) we'll circulate to procurement.

—Olivia
Head of Product, Finora Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Model shortlist + trial plan: tradeoffs & next steps (Finora constraints)

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Finora's clarifying notes. Key constraints: p95 <= 300ms for chat; $12k/month trial budget; must minimize hallucination for regulatory summaries. Procurement will ask for SOC 2 evidence.

My proposed technical plan (actionable):
- Default: redwood-lite-6b-quant, tuned with our prefix caching and small-kv-cache for retrieval hits. Expected p95 ~180–220ms under their expected qps.
- Canary: redwood-mid-13b-opt at 20% traffic for 72h. We'll instrument the canary with the following metrics: ROUGE-L, F1 on labeled prompts, hallucination_count (manual labeling + simple entity fate check), avg_tokens_per_call, p50/p95 latency, and error_rate.
- Fallback routing: route intent tag "regulatory_summary" to redwood-qa-33b with strict rate caps; track fallback_rate and cost delta.
- Monitoring & alerts: set up regression alerts if ROUGE-L drops >5% vs baseline or hallucination_count increases by 33% in a 24h window.

Operational asks for Ben: estimate monthly spend given their $12k target. Use our cost model with assumptions: baseline traffic X (they'll share sample), canary 20%, fallback 5% of calls. Please prepare two options: Dedicated reserved capacity estimate and Hosted pay-as-you-go for the trial.

Karthik — can you prepare the bench config and the prompt-set pass/fail scripts? I attached the prompt sets and bench CSV. We'll need the 48-hour throughput run once they share the dataset.

I'll draft a short monitoring doc to send with the next email to Finora (include SOC 2 evidence link).

Thanks —
Marissa

Olivia / Peter —

Following up with a tightened plan based on your SLO and budget. Summary below and exact asks so procurement can move forward.

Summary of the proposed trial (short):
- Default: redwood-lite-6b-quant (expected p95 ~200ms)
- Canary: redwood-mid-13b-opt on 20% traffic for 72 hours to collect quality metrics
- Fallback: redwood-qa-33b for intent-tagged regulatory summaries (we'll start with a 5% cap)
- Monitoring: ROUGE-L / F1 on labeled prompts, hallucination_count, p95 latency, tokens/call. Regression alert: ROUGE-L drop >5% or hallucination_count +33% over baseline triggers rollback.

Procurement & compliance items included: 
- SOC 2 evidence: https://redwood.app/compliance/soc2 (public SSP + contact)
- DocuSign trial PO template: https://redwood.app/hubspot/deal/DEAL-4579-FIN/docuSign

Concrete asks for Finora:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the trial config (default + canary + fallback) and the $12k/month budget target.
2) Share a redacted sample dataset (500–1,000 rows) by Tue May 31 so we can run the 48-hour bench.
3) Provide a primary technical contact to receive test API keys and monitor canary metrics (we recommend Olivia or an eng lead).

If you confirm, we will:
- Spin up the trial environment and send test keys within 24 hours of dataset upload
- Run the 48-hour bench and return an expected monthly cost estimate (hosted and dedicated)
- Schedule a 45-min sync Tue Jun 1 to review bench results and decide on any model/fallback tuning

Attachments for your reference: trial-config.yaml (routing rules + traffic split), finora-benchmarks-20270525.csv, finora-demo-screen.mp4

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Best,
